messages:
alex: Heads-up — our SCIM backfill job from last night ran against the old role-mapping and added ~120 users to `infra-admins` in prod. Not a graceful mapping, looks like a rewrite + backfill race.

riley: ugh. how did it run? I thought the migration was gated.

alex: migration deploy had a stale flag flip on the cron worker. The backfill kicked off at ~02:15 UTC. I pulled audit: `SELECT user_id, group, src, ts FROM scim_audit WHERE ts BETWEEN 2067888000 AND 2067890400 AND change_type='group_membership'`

riley: paste the top 10? any service accounts included?

alex: pasted snippet in thread (ids redacted). 3 service accounts affected, ~15 users with SSO only, rest are org users.

sana: tagging kms-sec — are any of the affected groups granting KMS key principals? If infra-admins maps to a key ACL we need immediate rotation or removal.

jordan: checking key ACLs now. infra-admins used in 2 KMS policies: `infra-ingest-key` and `infra-managed-kms`. Both grant decrypt/describe to group principal.

infra-bot: incident created: INC-2026-456 — SCIM backfill misapply. Pager duty notified.

riley: containment plan: 1) pause SCIM sync (cron and webhook) 2) remove group bindings that are wrong 3) revoke service tokens for affected service accounts 4) audit logs and notify customers if needed. Thoughts?

sana: agree. add: rotate the KMS grants for those keys (create new key version / rekey) OR remove group principal references immediately from key policy. Rotating is heavier; removing group principal buys time.

alex: I'm pausing the cron now. Patch deploy id `deploy-2026-03-scim-fix`.

jordan: removing group principals from `infra-managed-kms` now (will patch key policy). I'll snapshot policy first and post diffs.

riley: start a short-lived rollback: run a targeted deprovision for the exact audit entries (we can script `scim:removeMember(user, infra-admins)` for the listed user_ids). Alex, can you generate the list?

alex: uploading user list to secure S3 path and sharing link in off-channel.

sana: also add an audit annotation to each deprov action so we can trace automatic vs manual. And file an RFC for stronger gating on backfills.

oncall-bot: @oncall-sec acknowledged. ETA 45m for initial containment.

riley: after containment let's run a conservative permission diff: compare effective RBAC for a random sample of 50 users vs a day ago. We'll surface any other unexpected grants.

jordan: key policy diff applied. Removed group principal from infra-managed-kms and infra-ingest-key. Will schedule rotation if we see suspicious access attempts.

alex: job to deprov started (batch size 50). I'll post progress updates.

sana: postmortem items: gating for backfill jobs, require dry-run opt-in, add explicit ACL checks for keys before group-to-key mapping, alert on >10 admin grants within 1h, and KMS policy change runbook.

riley: good. once all deprovs done we'll re-enable sync with a flag to skip backfill.

alex: update — batch 3/3 complete. 119 users removed from infra-admins, 3 svc-accounts rotated tokens.

jordan: no anomalous decrypt events in the last 6h. Still monitoring.

riley: closing incident when we've had 24h clean and postmortem created. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
